nodes.title: Energy Bands & Classification of Solids
points: Valence Band (VB): Lower energy band completely or partially filled with valence electrons; conduction cannot occur in completely filled VB.
Conduction Band (CB): Higher energy band, either empty or partially filled; electrons in CB are free electrons responsible for electrical conduction.
Forbidden Energy Gap (Bandgap E_g): Energy separation between top of VB and bottom of CB. No allowed electron energy states exist in E_g.
Conductors (Metals): VB and CB overlap, or CB is partially filled (E_g ≈ 0). Abundant free electrons at all temperatures.
Semiconductors: Small bandgap (E_g < 3 eV, e.g., Silicon E_g ≈ 1.1 eV, Germanium E_g ≈ 0.7 eV at 300 K). Insulator at 0 K, conducts at room temperature.
Insulators: Very large bandgap (E_g > 3 eV, e.g., Diamond E_g ≈ 5.4 eV). Electrons cannot jump from VB to CB.

nodes.title: Intrinsic & Extrinsic Semiconductors (Doping)
points: Intrinsic Semiconductor: Pure semiconductor (pure Si or Ge). Thermal energy generates equal number of electrons in CB and holes in VB: n_e = n_h = n_i.
Extrinsic Semiconductor: Semiconductor doped with small controlled amount of impurity atoms (~1 in 10⁶) to greatly increase conductivity.

n-type Semiconductor: Doped with Pentavalent impurity (P, As, Sb). Impurity atom donates an extra conduction electron (Donor atom). Majority carriers = Electrons (n_e ≫ n_h); Minority carriers = Holes.

p-type Semiconductor: Doped with Trivalent impurity (B, Al, Ga, In). Impurity atom creates an electron vacancy/hole (Acceptor atom). Majority carriers = Holes (n_h ≫ n_e); Minority carriers = Electrons.
Electrical Neutrality: Both n-type and p-type semiconductors are strictly ELECTRICALLY NEUTRAL.
Mass-Action Law: Under thermal equilibrium, product of electron and hole concentrations is constant: n_e × n_h = n_i².

formulas.label: Total current
formulas.expr: I = I_e + I_h = e A (n_e v_e + n_h v_h)

nodes.title: p-n Junction Diode Formation & Depletion Layer
points: Formation: When a p-type semiconductor is joined to an n-type crystal, majority electrons diffuse from n to p and holes diffuse from p to n (Diffusion Current).

Depletion Layer: Region on either side of junction depleted of mobile charge carriers, containing only immobile positive donor ions on n-side and immobile negative acceptor ions on p-side. Width ≈ 0.5 μm.
Barrier Potential (V_B): Built-in potential difference across depletion layer opposing further diffusion: V_B ≈ 0.7 V for Silicon; V_B ≈ 0.3 V for Germanium at room temperature.
Drift Current: Minority carriers swept across the junction by the internal electric field; at equilibrium: Diffusion Current = Drift Current (net current = 0).

nodes.title: Diode Biasing & I–V Characteristics
points: Forward Bias: p-region connected to positive terminal, n-region to negative terminal. External field opposes barrier potential, reducing depletion layer width.
After forward voltage exceeds Knee Voltage (Cut-in voltage V_k ≈ 0.7 V for Si, 0.3 V for Ge), forward current increases exponentially (measured in milliamperes, mA).
Reverse Bias: p-region connected to negative terminal, n-region to positive terminal. External field reinforces barrier potential, widening depletion layer.
A tiny, temperature-dependent reverse saturation current flows due to minority carriers (measured in microamperes, μA for Ge, nanoamperes, nA for Si).
Reverse Breakdown: At high reverse voltage (Breakdown voltage V_br), current increases drastically.
Static (DC) resistance R_dc = V / I; Dynamic (AC) resistance r_ac = ΔV / ΔI.

nodes.title: Diode Rectifiers: Half-Wave, Full-Wave & Filters
points: Half-Wave Rectifier (HWR): Uses 1 diode. Conducts only during positive half cycles of AC input. DC output V_dc = V_m / π ≈ 0.318 V_m; Ripple factor r = 1.21; Maximum efficiency η_max = 40.6%; Ripple frequency = f_in.

Full-Wave Rectifier (FWR - Centre-Tapped / Bridge): Conducts during both positive and negative half cycles. DC output V_dc = 2 V_m / π ≈ 0.636 V_m; Ripple factor r = 0.48; Maximum efficiency η_max = 81.2%; Ripple frequency = 2 f_in.
Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV): PIV = V_m (HWR and Bridge FWR); PIV = 2 V_m (Centre-tapped FWR).
Capacitor Filter: Shunt capacitor C connected across load R_L bypasses AC ripples. Ripple factor r ≈ 1 / (4√3 f C R_L).

nodes.title: Zener Diode as a Voltage Regulator
points: A Zener diode is a heavily doped silicon p-n junction diode designed to operate specifically in the REVERSE BREAKDOWN region without damage.
Heavily doped ⟹ Very thin depletion layer (~10⁻⁷ m) ⟹ High junction electric field (~10⁶ V/m) causing Zener breakdown at low reverse voltage.
Key Property: In reverse breakdown region, voltage across Zener diode remains constant (V_Z) over a wide range of reverse current.
Voltage Regulator Circuit: Unregulated DC input V_in connected to series resistance R_s and Zener diode in parallel with load R_L.
Current equation: I_s = I_Z + I_L, where I_s = (V_in − V_Z) / R_s and I_L = V_Z / R_L.
If V_in increases: V_Z remains constant; excess voltage drops across R_s; Zener current I_Z absorbs excess current.

nodes.title: Special Purpose Diodes: Photodiode, LED & Solar Cell
points: Photodiode: Special p-n junction operated in REVERSE BIAS. When light of energy hν > E_g strikes depletion layer, electron-hole pairs are generated, increasing reverse saturation current. Reverse current is directly proportional to incident light intensity. Used in optical detectors and lux meters.

Light Emitting Diode (LED): Heavily doped p-n junction operated in FORWARD BIAS. Electrons and holes recombine near junction, releasing energy as photons (hν ≈ E_g). Made from compound semiconductors (GaAsP, GaP) to emit visible light. Advantage: fast response, low power, long life.

Solar Cell: p-n junction operating on photovoltaic effect with NO EXTERNAL BIAS. Converts sunlight directly into electrical energy. Generates Open Circuit Voltage (V_oc) and Short Circuit Current (I_sc). Operates in the FOURTH QUADRANT of I–V characteristic curve.

nodes.title: Logic Gates, Truth Tables & De Morgan's Laws
points: Basic Gates: NOT Gate (Inverter: Y = Ā); AND Gate (Y = A · B); OR Gate (Y = A + B).
Universal Gates: NAND Gate [Y = ¬(A · B)]; NOR Gate [Y = ¬(A + B)]. Any Boolean function can be implemented using only NAND or only NOR gates.
Exclusive-OR (XOR Gate): Y = A ⊕ B = A B̄ + Ā B (high when inputs are distinct).
De Morgan's First Theorem: ¬(A + B) = Ā · B̄ (Complement of sum equals product of complements).
De Morgan's Second Theorem: ¬(A · B) = Ā + B̄ (Complement of product equals sum of complements).

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Questions & Rectifier Comparisons
points: Board Favourite #1: Explain working of Full-Wave Rectifier with neat circuit diagram and input-output waveforms.
Board Favourite #2: Explain working of Zener Diode as a Voltage Regulator with neat circuit diagram and I–V characteristic curve.
Board Favourite #3: Distinguish between Half-Wave and Full-Wave Rectifiers (Diodes: 1 vs 2/4; Efficiency: 40.6% vs 81.2%; Ripple factor: 1.21 vs 0.48; Ripple frequency: f vs 2f).
Board Favourite #4: State and prove De Morgan's theorems using truth tables.
Board Favourite #5: Distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, and between n-type and p-type semiconductors.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Logic Gate Traps & Zener Hacks
points: Ripple Frequency Shortcut: For 50 Hz input AC: HWR output ripple frequency = 50 Hz; FWR output ripple frequency = 2 × 50 = 100 Hz.

Biasing Trap: Photodiode is ALWAYS operated in REVERSE BIAS (fractional change in reverse current is far easier to measure). LED is ALWAYS operated in FORWARD BIAS. Solar cell requires ZERO external bias.
Zener Regulation Condition Trap: For Zener regulation to work, V_in MUST be greater than V_Z, and Zener current I_Z must not exceed maximum rated power dissipation P_Z(max) = V_Z × I_Z(max).
Minimum NAND Gates Required: NOT = 1 NAND; AND = 2 NANDs; OR = 3 NANDs; NOR = 4 NANDs; XOR = 4 NANDs; XNOR = 5 NANDs.
Minimum NOR Gates Required: NOT = 1 NOR; OR = 2 NORs; AND = 3 NORs; NAND = 4 NORs; XOR = 5 NORs; XNOR = 4 NORs.
